chunks: What al-Shaykh—may Allah the Exalted support him—informed me of, from Abū al-Qāsim Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb, from ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from Ismāʿīl ibn Marrār, from Yūnus, from some of his men, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

“The minimum period of purity is ten days. That is because when a woman first begins menstruating, she may at times have abundant blood, so her menstruation may be ten days. Then it continues to decrease as she grows older until it returns to three days. When it has returned to three days, her menstruation has risen, and it is not less than three days. So when a woman sees blood during the days of her menstruation, she leaves the salat (prayer). If the blood continues with her for three days, then she is menstruating. But if the blood stops after she has seen it for one day or two days, she performs ghusl (ritual bath), prays, and waits from the day she saw the blood up to ten days. Then if she sees, within those ten days from the day she saw the blood, for one day or two days until it completes three days for her, then what she saw at the beginning together with what she saw afterward within the ten days is from menstruation. But if ten days pass from the day she saw it and she does not see blood, then that one day or two days which she saw was not from menstruation; rather it was from an ailment, either from a sore in the interior or from the interior. So she must repeat the salat (prayer) of those two days which she left, because she was not menstruating. Thus it is obligatory upon her to make up what she left of the salat (prayer) on that one day or two days. And if three days are completed for her, then it is from menstruation, and that is the minimum menstruation, and make-up is not obligatory upon her. And the period of purity is not less than ten days. So if a woman menstruates and her menstruation is five days, then the blood stops, she performs ghusl (ritual bath) and prays. Then if she sees blood after that, and ten days have not been completed for her from the day she became pure, then that is from menstruation, and she leaves the salat (prayer). But if from the first of what she saw to the second that she saw, ten complete days are reached, and it continues with her, she counts from the first blood and the second blood ten days, then after that she is a mustaḥāḍah, and she does what the mustaḥāḍah does.”

And he said: “Whatever yellowish discharge or redness a woman sees during the days of her menstruation is from menstruation, and whatever she sees after the days of her menstruation is not from menstruation.”

key_terms.اغْتَسَلَتْ: she performed ghusl (ritual bath) after cessation of blood
key_terms.الطُّهْرِ: the state of purity between menstrual periods
key_terms.الْقَضَاءُ: making up missed acts of worship, here missed salat (prayer)
key_terms.الْمُسْتَحَاضَةُ: a woman in the state of istiḥāḍah, irregular non-menstrual bleeding
key_terms.حَائِضٌ: a menstruating woman subject to the rulings of ḥayḍ
key_terms.حَيْضُهَا: her menstruation; menstrual bleeding treated as ḥayḍ
key_terms.حُمْرَةٍ: reddish discharge considered in determining menstruation
key_terms.صُفْرَةٍ: yellowish discharge seen during or after the menstrual period

ai.seo_question: What are the rulings for minimum menstruation and minimum purity between periods in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith explains the legal rulings of menstruation, istiḥāḍah, and the minimum period of purity between menstrual cycles. It sets out how blood is to be counted within ten days, when salat (prayer) is left or resumed, and when missed prayers must be made up.
